subject: SIG follow-up: dataflow & retention details for evidence
summary: Acme requested clarification on where logs and backups are stored, retention windows by region, and whether archived logs include PKI chain evidence. We agreed to upload a dataflow diagram, SOC2 snapshot, and KMS rotation logs to our Whistic/Vendr profile and provided target dates for evidence delivery.
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: dataflow & retention details for evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for starting the SIG/QnA import into our portal. A couple of items our security team needs to close the assessment:

- A clear dataflow graphic showing where customer request/response payloads, logs, and backups reside (S3 buckets, regions), including any caching layers (prefix/KV cache).
- Retention policy for runtime logs vs. backups and whether backups are stored cross-region or encrypted with customer-specific keys.
- If archived logs are used to investigate incidents, do they include the full PKI chain / signature verification artifacts?

If you can upload those items to your Whistic/Vendr profile or attach here, that should get us most of the way. Also include any SOC 2 evidence snapshot or a link to a signed attestation.

Can you confirm a target by end of next week (2025-06-17)?

Best,
Lara
Lara Chen
Senior Security Engineer, Acme Corp
acme-security@acme.com

---
Attachment: none (please upload to profile)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: dataflow & retention details for evidence

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I’ll follow with attachments and a short plan for upload: 

- Dataflow: we’ll provide a PDF diagram that maps user request -> edge routing -> inference runtime -> KV/prefix cache -> response, plus where logs and backups are written (S3 buckets, region tags). We will annotate which queues are encrypted at rest and which use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).
- Retention: runtime request/trace logs: default 30 days (configurable per customer), archived backups: 365 days by default for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private customers can set retention per contract. We’ll include the retention matrix by region (US, EU, APAC).
- Archived logs & PKI artifacts: archived incident records include signature verification records and certificate chains where applicable; we store signature metadata and timestamping to allow replay verification. We will include an example export of a verified audit record.

Action plan: I’ll upload the dataflow PDF, a SOC 2 evidence snapshot, and a KMS rotation log extract to our Whistic profile and share links by 2025-06-12 EOD. If you prefer Vendr or OneTrust links instead, say the word and we’ll push there too.

Attaching a draft dataflow (placeholder) to this reply — final will include bucket names redacted for public docs.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (draft)

Marissa — forwarding Lara. Suggested items to include in the upload (short checklist):

* redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (annotate regions + KMS vs service keys)
* soc2-snapshot-202504.zip (encrypted, access-controlled)
* kms-rotation-log.csv (last 6 rotations, timezone + operator)

If Rishi approves, I can kick off the upload to Whistic and tag the files as 'Evidence: retention, encryption, PKI'.

-kim

Hi Lara — following up with the deliverables we discussed. Links/attachments below. Let me know if you want us to upload the same package to Vendr or OneTrust.

Uploaded evidence (Whistic profile): https://whistic.com/profiles/redwood-inference 
- redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (final, annotated; regions redacted for public view, full map shared in private bundle)
- soc2-snapshot-202504.zip (contains SOC 2 attestations and control mappings; access limited)
- kms-rotation-log.csv (CSV extract - shows last 6 rotations, key IDs redacted)
- example-archive-audit.json (sanitized; demonstrates PKI chain & signature verification steps)

Short answers reiterated:
- Runtime/trace logs: default 30 days; archived incident logs retained 365 days and include verification artifacts.
- Backups: encrypted at rest; default cross-region replication disabled for hosted profiles; Dedicated/Private customers can enable cross-region per contract.
- Customer-managed KMS: available for Dedicated/Private deployments; for hosted API we offer KMS integrations (bring-your-own-key options) for enterprise customers.

If Acme needs the full S3 bucket names and object paths to run a bucket-level reconciliation, we can provision limited access via our secure evidence-sharing flow — we’d need an approved PO or NDA first.

Next steps: confirm whether you need the private bundle in OneTrust/Vendr and a date to give Acme read access (we can do 2025-06-16 if that works).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Security Programs Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
